children: , Nvidia's rising challenger in AI infrastructure, climbed approximately 3.5% to $523.58 Wednesday, extending Tuesday's rally. Chief Financial Officer Jean Hu sees the market available to AMD reaching between $2 trillion and $3 trillion by 2030a staggering prize even for the industry's biggest chipmakers.

The company is already accelerating. AMD's second-quarter results showed revenue jumping 50% to $11.54 billion, while data-center revenue more than doubled to $6.7 billion and generated roughly 58% of total sales. Management now expects third-quarter revenue of approximately $13 billion.

The valuation picture shows how much optimism is already baked in: the chart places AMD's $523.58 share price 87.56% above its GF Value estimate of $279.15. Meanwhile, even the low end of Hu's market estimate is more than 43 times AMD's annualized second-quarter revenuebut addressable market is opportunity, not guaranteed sales. AMD still must secure enough advanced manufacturing capacity, expand Instinct deployments and defend margins to turn that enormous runway into lasting shareholder returns.

title: AMD Jumps 3.5% as Its $2 Trillion-Plus AI Promise Raises the Stakes
